correctness.rationale: FO2 two-pebble relation records precisely atomic pair type relative to one stationary vertex: equality, each labeled forward/reverse generator edge, and whether a generic vertex exists. Left translations make every type realizable uniformly; a back-and-forth system proves indefinite equivalence, while explicit FO2 sentences test all signed-list coincidences/η. FO3 balanced recursion for word paths P_w(x,y) uses three reusable variables with quantifier rank <=ceil(log2 length), hence 3-variable sentences detect all word relations and identify the free-group kernel/marked quotient. The finite rank upper bound follows from a signed word p_a of length <=D representing each element in smaller group and relators p_a s p_as^-1 of length <=2D+1; if all hold in larger group they produce a surjective marked homomorphism of impossible size. Directed cyclic three-pebble gap game provides logarithmic lower bound. Independently checked signed-type equality and commutator separation for marked S3 and C6 and cyclic generic η boundary.

value.rationale: A strong natural finite-model-theoretic threshold for the standard edge-colored relational model of finite marked groups: two variables see only radius-one signed incidences, whereas a third recovers full group presentation with optimal logarithmic rank order. The same-cardinality S3/C6 witness exposes genuine expressive-width geometry, not a routine finite class table.
residual_risks: General colored/connected Cayley literature may already imply parts of the 3-variable word-language construction; unrestricted 2-variable classification and precise diameter-sensitive rank remain the substantive features.

final_claim: For finite d-marked connected directed Cayley relational structures, unbounded-depth FO2-equivalence is precisely equality of signed-list equality partition π and generic-element bit η; FO3-equivalence is marked-group isomorphism, with distinguishing 3-variable rank logarithmic in the smaller signed-generator diameter and a sharp cyclic lower-order example.
limitations: Only finite, connected, position-labeled generator-edge relational Cayley digraphs; no unlabeled, uncolored, disconnected or ternary group-multiplication languages.
Oxford institutional VPN disconnected for directly relevant 2005 Kuske–Lohrey primary full text; originality remains qualified.
